blocks.text: Banking built for people who have just arrived

blocks.html: A German account without the German paperwork.

Student, employee, job seeker or simply starting over: everyone who moves to Germany needs a local account that just works. Landlords and employers ask for a German IBAN, and paying with a foreign card gets expensive quickly.

With EC Assets you skip the branch visit and the forms and get an account that is designed around the first year in a new country. Receive your salary, pay your rent and shop without foreign transaction fees.

Open your Blocked Account and your Bank Account in the same application, and add the health insurance your visa requires, all within a few minutes, through the {{product}}.

You will not need a second German account.

items.q: What is the difference between the Blocked Account and the Bank Account?
items.a:
The Blocked Account is for your visa; the Bank Account is for daily life.

Blocked Account:
It holds the deposit that proves your funds to the German authorities. The money is released to you in monthly instalments after you arrive, which is why it is called blocked.

Bank Account:
A current account (Girokonto) for rent, groceries, insurance premiums and salary. It comes with a digital debit card, and a physical card is available on request.

After arrival, your monthly payout moves automatically from the Blocked Account to the Bank Account.

With EC Assets you get both, so there is no need to open another German account.

items.q: Why do I need this account?
items.a:
To receive your monthly Blocked Account payouts and to pay for health insurance, rent and everyday costs while you are in Germany.

It is a German account with a German IBAN, which landlords, employers and insurers will ask for.

Using a local account also avoids the transaction fees and friction that come with paying from a foreign card.

Yes.
